title: Ang 1107–1110: Nanak's twelve months
tomorrow: what do you do with a night that won't end?

cards: A countdown app on a phone: so many days until graduation, until the move, until the trip. Every time you open it, the number is smaller, and somehow that feels both exciting and sad.
Guru Nanak wrote a different kind of calendar. It opens raga Tukhari on ang 1107, and it's called Barah Maha, the twelve months. It isn't a countdown.
It walks through the year one month at a time, and every month is a letter to someone you love.

teach.b: Barah Maha is a song form that moves through the months, each with its own weather and feeling. In Guru Nanak's, the voice is a bride longing for her Beloved, the One. Each season says something about that longing.
Spring, in paraphrase: Chet is lovely, the bumblebees hum, the woods are in flower, but how can I be happy without my Love at home? Then the heat, the rains, the frost.

Every month, the same question: is the Beloved near? What's surprising is the ending. In paraphrase: the twelve months, the seasons, the days and the moments are all blessed, when the True One comes and meets with ease.
So the calendar isn't good months and bad months.
Any month can turn out blessed. It depends on whether the Beloved is close, not on the weather. That changes how you hold a countdown.
The number still gets smaller. But a month isn't only a step toward the end. Each one is its own letter, and it can hold its own meeting.
Guru Arjan wrote a twelve-month song too, much earlier in the Granth, in Majh.

how: Guru Nanak's Barah Maha in raga Tukhari is sung in kirtan and read in order in a complete reading of the Guru Granth Sahib.

games.q: your friend's partner moved across the country for a year. she says the months apart are just time to get through. what would Nanak's months say?
o: each month can hold its own meeting; it isn't only a step to the end.
longing is weakness, so try to stop missing him.
only the month he comes back will count for anything.
games.why: the song's ending blesses every month, season and moment when the Beloved is near: the calendar isn't only a countdown.

practice: Go back through the last twelve months in your mind, one finger for each. For every month, find one moment when someone you love felt close. If a month comes up empty, just let it pass and move to the next.
